chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Overview
Kathmandu University's undergraduate admission for the 2026/2027 academic year in btech in Artificial Students covers the School of Engineering (SoE). Applicants must apply and sit the KUCAT-CBT entrance test before being considered for admission.

chunks.heading: Who can apply?
chunks.text:
Who can apply?
The admission is open for Nepalese as well as foreign students.

chunks.heading: Key Dates and Deadlines
chunks.text:
Key Dates and Deadlines
The application notice was published on June 17, 2026. Online registration opened June 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM and closes July 9, 2026 at midnight (Nepal time, UTC+5:45). Form filling and payment must be completed by July 10, 2026. These dates apply specifically to the 2026/2027 cycle and may be revised — any schedule change is announced on the KU website, so callers asking about deadlines should be pointed there or to the admission office if there's any doubt the date has shifted.

chunks.heading: Before Applying > Registration Window
chunks.text:
Before Applying > Registration Window
Applications for admission and the KUCAT-CBT 2026 entrance test are submitted entirely through the online portal. Online form registration is only open from June 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM to July 9, 2026 at midnight (Nepal time, UTC+5:45) — applications cannot be submitted outside this window.

chunks.heading: Before Applying > What to Check Before Starting the Form
chunks.text:
Before Applying > What to Check Before Starting the Form
Before filling out the application, applicants should first understand their intended program, its eligibility criteria, and the subject area they plan to apply for, including the specific admission requirements and qualifications needed for that program.

chunks.heading: Before Applying > Where to Get Program Information
chunks.text:
Before Applying > Where to Get Program Information
Program and subject area details are available on the School of Engineering website at soe.ku.edu.np, or the School of Science website at sos.ku.edu.np. Applicants can also visit KU's main campus in Dhulikhel and contact the relevant department or the Dean's office directly.

chunks.heading: Before Applying > Deadlines to Track
chunks.text:
Before Applying > Deadlines to Track
Applicants should note the online application deadline, their preferred test center, and any other scheduled activities before beginning the application, since these dates and options are set in advance and are not adjustable per applicant.

chunks.heading: How to Apply
chunks.text:
How to Apply
Applications are submitted entirely online at apply.ku.edu.np/cbt, and a valid email address is required. Applicants first register with their name, email, and a password, then must click the confirmation link and enter the confirmation code sent by email before continuing. Once logged in, applicants fill in personal and academic details, select exactly one program and subject area, upload a passport-style photo and a valid identification document, and upload any other required documents. Information can be saved and edited at any point — but once the documents and payment proof are uploaded and the form is submitted, no further changes are possible.

chunks.heading: Accepted Identification Documents
chunks.text:
Accepted Identification Documents
A valid personal identification document with the applicant's photo is required, and the original must be produced later at the entrance test and admission if offered. Accepted documents are: a citizenship certificate, a passport with a valid date, the admit card from the final class 12 (or equivalent) examination, a driving license with a valid date, or a national ID.

chunks.heading: Application Fee and Payment
chunks.text:
Application Fee and Payment
The application processing fee is NRs. 2,000 (two thousand Nepalese rupees), paid only through eSewa. This fee is strictly non-refundable and non-transferable — this applies even if a candidate does not appear for the entrance test, is not offered admission, or if the test format later changes. Payments made to any other university account are not considered valid, and the admission committee is not responsible for refunding those.

chunks.heading: Admission Card
chunks.text:
Admission Card
After the fee is paid, applicants can log back into the application portal to download and print their admission card. It must be printed in color, and the candidate must bring it along with their original identification document to the entrance exam.

chunks.heading: Entrance Exam (KUCAT-CBT)
chunks.text:
Entrance Exam (KUCAT-CBT)
The KUCAT-CBT entrance test is a computer-based test taken in person — it is not available online. The test schedule is published separately on the KU website and application portal, and once scheduled, there is no rescheduling of the date or time. Candidates should arrive at the exam center well ahead of time and be at the exam room at least 30 minutes before the test starts, bringing both the printed admission card and the original identification document used during application. Personal calculators are not allowed; a calculator is available on the exam computer if needed. Mobile phones and other portable electronic devices are strictly prohibited in the exam room.

chunks.heading: Entrance Exam (KUCAT-CBT)
chunks.text:
Entrance Exam (KUCAT-CBT)

chunks.heading: After the Exam
chunks.text:
After the Exam
Candidates can check their KUCAT-CBT score after the test. Results and further admission notices are published on the KU website, and the actual admission offer process is handled separately by the Admission Committees under SoE .

chunks.heading: Foreign Nationals
chunks.text:
Foreign Nationals
Foreign nationals are eligible to apply for admission provided they meet all minimum requirements. Applicants in this situation should contact the school of engineering dministration directly for specific guidance.

chunks.heading: Refunds
chunks.text:
Refunds
The application fee is non-refundable and non-transferable under all circumstances described in the official procedure - including if the candidate misses the entrance test, is not offered admission, or if the test's mode or format changes. There is no exception process described for this fee.

chunks.heading: Getting Help
chunks.text:
Getting Help
For problems or confusion while filling out the online application, applicants can email admission@ku.edu.np. Response times can take several hours to several days given the volume of queries, so this should be set as the expectation when directing a caller to email rather than call back immediately.

chunks.heading: Application Appendix > Photo Requirements
chunks.text:
Application Appendix > Photo Requirements
The photo uploaded with the application must be a recent, color photo of the candidate, with the face clearly visible against a light, plain background, covering at least 50 to 60 percent of the image. The file size must not exceed 500 KB. The entrance and admission committees reserve the right to reject a candidate if the submitted photo is too old or no longer resembles their current appearance.

chunks.heading: Application Appendix > Document Upload Requirements
chunks.text:
Application Appendix > Document Upload Requirements
Scanned documents uploaded with the application must be clear, readable, and fully visible, with each file no larger than 500 KB. The details on the document must match what the candidate entered in the application form, and the original document must be produced later if admission is offered. The entrance and admission committees can reject a candidate if the uploaded copy doesn't match the original, or if there's a major discrepancy between the form details and the submitted or original documents.

chunks.heading: Application Appendix > One Application, One Attempt Rule
chunks.text:
Application Appendix > One Application, One Attempt Rule
Each candidate is allowed only one application and one attempt at the KUCAT-CBT 2026 entrance exam. If a candidate is found to have submitted multiple applications — whether using the same or a different identification document — or appears in the exam more than once, all of their exam attempts will be cancelled and they will be disqualified from the admission process entirely.
